text:
maria: Heads-up — starting SEA2 bring-up run. Goal: validate kernel/driver interop + synthetic network/throughput baselines before handing off to SRE. P95 target for short seq (<=512) is 80ms. Can folks help with checks and any known sea2 quirks?

kai: on it. I'll run kernel/driver sweep and nvlink checks on the first rack. ETA 30m.

jess: noted. I'll prepare a redwood-bench workload: short-seq-512, long-seq-2048, and an embeddings steady-state. Will push configs to /opt/redwood/tests/sea2/bench-configs.

andrew: reminder: SEA region has 25Gb interconnect on these hosts, not 100Gb. Expect higher tail if batching >4. Documenting cost/perf tradeoff now.

maria: thanks. runbook (high level):
1) bootstrap nodes: bios settings, grub kernel args (mitigate c-states)
2) install drivers: nvidia-driver 535.xx, cuda 12.2, gcc toolchain pinned
3) kernel module sanity: modinfo nvidia && dmesg | grep -i nvidia
4) nvlink validation: nvlink status + nvlink-metrics check
5) network synthetic: iperf3 across racks, somaxconn probes, tc qdisc defaults
6) redwood-bench perf sweep + p95 baseline
7) capture traces and upload to bench-bucket
8) handoff checklist to eng-sre

kai: doing step 3 now. quick checks:
- ssh root@sea2-rack01-gn03
- nvidia-smi -q | head -n 30
- cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
- lsmod | grep nvidia

kai: found one node with 'NVRM: Xid 79' in dmesg. tagging it. Possible driver mismatch on one host. Will re-provision kernel-headers and reinstall.

jess: deploying bench config to the cluster:
```
# /opt/redwood/tests/sea2/bench-configs/short-seq-512.yaml
workload: generation
model: redwood-open-13b-v1
sequence_length: 512
batch_sizes: [1,2,4]
steady_state_seconds: 600
metrics: [p50,p90,p95,p99,throughput]
```

jess: note — start with batch 1 then sweep. On sea2 remember to set BATCHER_MAX_DELAY_MS=4 to keep latency SLO.

andrew: net checks in parallel:
- iperf3 -c sea2-rack02-gn01 -P8 -t60
- ethtool -S ens5 | grep tx_errors
- tc -s qdisc show dev ens5

andrew: iperf3 between rack01 and rack02: 22.7 Gbits/sec with 8 streams. within spec for 25Gb links, margin ~2.3 Gbps.

kai: reinstalled driver on one host, rebooted. dmesg now clean for nvidia. nvlink lanes all up on rack01. running nvlink-sanity: PASS.

sasha: small note on kernel version: stock distro kernel 6.1.45 had one regression with page-migration and cuda pinned pages — we recommend 6.1.52 on these builds. I'll push kernel upgrade to the image used by sea2 nodes.

maria: thanks — please log the kernel image version in the bench artifacts. Also set a tag sea2-kernel=6.1.52 if upgraded.

jess: redwood-bench results first sweep (batch=1, seq=512):
- rack01 node0: p95=74ms, p99=120ms, throughput=420 tok/s
- rack01 node1: p95=78ms, p99=130ms, throughput=410 tok/s
- rack02 (same hw): p95=82ms, p99=145ms, throughput=390 tok/s

jess: Rack02 tail is a bit high — correlating with wire-level drops? putting net trace capture on.

andrew: checked ethtool stats on rack02 node0: tx_errors incrementing slowly on ens5. Suspect faulty SFP or cabling at TOR. Opening ticket with colo ops.

infra-oncall: ticket COLO-SEA2-403 opened for TOR port flapping. Assigned to colo-tech. ETA for patch: 2 hours.

maria: action item: mark rack02 nodes as canary until link is confirmed healthy. Manual routing: set routing policy to prefer rack01 for latency-sensitive traffic.

jess: after removing rack02 from canary set, short-seq p95 aggregated across canary nodes = 76ms, p99=125ms. Throughput baseline for sea2 canary: 415 tok/s avg per GPU for short seq.

maria: cost note — at these numbers we estimate $0.0009 per token for short-seq at current instance pricing and batch/kv cache settings. We'll include that in handoff doc under cost-impact.

kai: next step: driver stress test overnight (12h) with mixed workloads + nvlink transfer exercise. I'll post logs to s3://redwood-bench/sea2/nightly/2165439876/.

maria: handoff checklist (for eng-sre):
- all nodes kernel >=6.1.52 and nvidia-driver 535.xx
- no NVRM Xid errors in dmesg last 24h
- nvlink lanes green on all nodes in canary
- net link errors = 0 for 1 hour after colo fix
- redwood-bench canonical p95 <=80ms short-seq
- artifacts uploaded to bench-bucket with tag sea2-2165439876
- cost estimate appended to ticket

andrew: adding an ops play: if TOR port flapping returns, drain affected node:
```
redwood infra drain-node --node <node-id> --reason "tor-flap"
ipmitool chassis power cycle <node>
```

maria: great. once kai finishes overnight stress and infra-oncall confirms net stable, i'll mark the run as ready for eng-sre handoff and create the handoff thread in #eng-sre.

deploy-bot: Deployment note: bench run finished. Artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-bench/sea2/2165439876/results.json

sasha: FYI I pushed an updated AMI with kernel 6.1.52 and pinned packages. Image id ami-0sea2-2165. Use when reprovisioning Rack02 after colo fix.

maria: thanks all. follow-ups: kai will post stress logs, colo will update ticket, jess will run a short regression tomorrow after colo confirms. I'll open handoff in #eng-sre once green. :thumbsup:

infra-oncall: COLO-SEA2-403 update: tech replaced SFP and patch cable, monitoring. No further tx_errors observed in the last 15min.

jess: quick regression after fix: rack02 p95 back to 77ms, throughput 405 tok/s. within variance.

maria: handoff ready. creating eng-sre thread now. Thanks everyone. :party:
